{{Vanilla|Enchanting#Enchantments|Enchantment}}
{{About|the list of enchantments|how enchantments are obtained and applied|Enchanting}}
An '''enchantment''' is a modifier on a piece of equipment or a book. [[Matcha Flavoured]] keeps the vanilla enchantments, changes a few of them, and adds eight enchantments of its own. Enchantments come from crafted [[blessing]]s, [[Ofuda]], loot and some pre-enchanted equipment rather than from an enchanting table. See [[Enchanting]] for how the system works.

The pack also uses enchantments for the fixed [[intrinsic]] effects of equipment ([[Warding]], [[Magic protection]], [[Cleanse]], [[Doom]] and the alloy intrinsics). Those have their own pages.

== Vanilla enchantments ==
Every vanilla enchantment is still in the game. The pack sets the anvil cost multiplier of all of them to 1 (the five that were already 1 are unchanged), which makes combining books in an [[anvil]] cheap. The substantive changes are to [[Feather Falling]], [[Fortune]] and [[Looting]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/enchantment/feather_falling.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/enchantment/fortune.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/enchantment/looting.json}}</ref> The pack's own enchantments add incompatibilities: [[Slaughter]] can't be combined with the damage enchantments, the [[magic protection]] of shakudo armor and the shakudo elytra can't be combined with the four protection enchantments, and the alloy tool intrinsics can't be combined with Fortune or Silk Touch.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/enchantment/slaughter.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/enchantment/magic_protection.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/enchantment/exclusive_set/mining.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/enchantment/exclusive_set/intrinsic_mining.json}}</ref> The pack also adds poisonous potatoes, the base item of most of its custom items, to the item tag of enchantable helmets, which the helmet and armor enchantments name as their supported items.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/tags/item/enchantable/head_armor.json}}</ref>

"Comes on" lists equipment that is crafted, traded or found with the enchantment already applied. "Random chest and fishing books" means books rolled from <code>#minecraft:on_random_loot</code> in dungeon, mineshaft, pyramid, stronghold, mansion, ocean ruin and ancient city chests and in fishing treasure (see [[Enchanting#Other sources]]). "Trial chamber vaults" means the fixed list of books in normal trial chamber reward vaults.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/trial_chambers/reward_rare.json}}</ref>

{{Data/Enchantments/Vanilla
|minecraft:feather_falling=Fall damage reduction doubled
}}

Blast Protection, Projectile Protection, Thorns, Sweeping Edge, Quick Charge and Curse of Vanishing have no blessing or trade. Apart from loot, four of them come only already applied to crafted gear: [[Sturdy leather armor|sturdy leather armor]] has Projectile Protection II–IV, [[Chainmail armor|chainmail armor]] has Thorns III, [[Steel equipment|steel armor]] has Blast Protection II–IV and the [[Shakudo Sword|shakudo sword]] has Sweeping Edge I. Quick Charge and Curse of Vanishing can only be found. Protection and Sharpness have no blessing: apart from loot, they come only from [[Ofuda]] and from [[Adamant equipment|adamant equipment]], which is smithed with Protection I or Sharpness I.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/sturdy_leather_boots.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/chainmail_chestplate.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/steel_chestplate.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/shakudo_sword.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/adamant_sword.json}}</ref>

== Generated data ==
The table below is generated from the pack's enchantment files. It also lists the intrinsic enchantments, whose names are the tooltip glyphs they show in game, and five enchantments left in the old <code>main</code> namespace. Those exist so that items from versions before {{Version|1.12.2}} can be converted: holding or wearing an item with a <code>main:</code> enchantment replaces it with the <code>matcha:</code> version, one level per tick. In 1.12.2 they are also what five [[blessing]]s give; see [[Blessing#Old enchantment ids]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/main/README.txt}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/main/item_modifier/update_reach.json}}</ref>
